questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Zimbabwe?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Zimbabwe article.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Zimbabwe?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Language” part of the Zimbabwe article.

questions.proof: The country Zimbabwe has a mixture of languages; Shona, Ndebele, Venda, Manyika, Nyanja, Chagani, and a unique-unified Zimbabwean English.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The countries that surround Zimbabwe are _____, Botswana, South Africa and Mozambique.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Botswana”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Zimbabwe article, under the heading “Geography”.

questions.proof: The countries that surround Zimbabwe are Zambia, Botswana, South Africa and Mozambique.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The area that is now Zimbabwe was added to the British Empire around _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the nineteenth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Zimbabwe article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: The area that is now Zimbabwe was added to the British Empire around 1890.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “African citizens were given full equality in _____, and the country's name was officially changed to Zimbabwe.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Zimbabwe article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: African citizens were given full equality in 1980, and the country's name was officially changed to Zimbabwe.
